pledge.text: 100% of net Purpose Fees go to the listed charities within 60 days of each payout, after published, capped costs: running costs at most 15% of a year's net fees, and the reserve at most 5% of each payout until it holds six months of costs, so at least 80% every year. Listed supporters lower the costs, never what is passed on. No cap is ever raised for a purchase already made. Every cost and transfer is published monthly.

notes: The badge is served from the live-status endpoint, so an expired or revoked Entitlement never keeps showing as valid; {status} is valid, expired or revoked. It carries no recipient name, no figure, no heart, no cross and no mark but the Purpose Source name, and it looks the same for every lane and every amount. It is proof of licence coverage and never a mark of social or charitable merit.
badge.euConsumerNotice: If you sell to consumers in the European Union: show the badge only beside information about the software you use and the licence it is under — never beside a claim about your social or environmental merit, and never as a trust or quality mark for your own products. From 2026-09-27, Directive (EU) 2024/825 blacklists displaying a sustainability label, environmental or social, that is not based on a certification scheme; this badge is not one, and it must not be shown as one.

rules.rule: Never call the Purpose Fee a donation, a gift, a contribution, sponsorship or tax-deductible, and never call your organisation a donor.
rules.reason: The fee is the price of a licence credential, and the Association's terms, invoices and tax position rest on that.

rules.rule: Print no number the Association did not print: no impact figure, outcome, beneficiary count or proportion before a disbursed row of the published ledger, and no “100%” or “80%” except inside the pledge's own words.
rules.reason: Nothing is presented as achieved before it is recorded, and a percentage taken out of its sentence says more than the pledge does.

rules.rule: Name no recipient organisation, and show no charity's logo, the red cross emblem or the words “Red Cross”; link the published Recipient List instead. Never say your fee supports a project, a maintainer or a contributor.
rules.reason: The names and emblems belong to others, some are protected by law, and no project or person ever receives any of the fee.

rules.rule: Speak about your own purchase only: never say that your customers' purchases, subscriptions or use support charity.
rules.reason: That is a charity promotion about your customers' money, which carries legal duties in several countries that this kit cannot meet for you.

rules.rule: Make no green, climate or sustainability claim about your organisation, your products or this purchase.
rules.reason: Swiss and European unfair-competition law require such claims to be substantiated to a standard this kit cannot give.

rules.rule: Never say that the Entitlement licenses the code, pays for the code or buys the software: it is a credential that meets a condition of the licence.
rules.reason: The Association is a registrar and never a party to any project's licence.

rules.rule: Say where the money goes only in the pledge's words: quote the Association's pledge exactly as written, or say nothing about the money and link where it goes. Never shorten, paraphrase or translate the pledge yourself.
rules.reason: The pledge is stated in one form only.

rules.rule: Use the give-something-back line only together with the pledge or the link to where the money goes; the generic “we support charity” framing stays excluded.
rules.reason: A giving line with nothing behind it is the vague claim these rules exist to stop.

rules.rule: Show the badge as proof of coverage, never as a mark of social or charitable merit.
rules.reason: See the note for consumer-facing organisations in the European Union.

rules.rule: Offer no verification address other than the one in each line: verify only at purposesource.org/verify.
rules.reason: One address is what makes a forged badge or certificate easy to spot.

a restated, shortened or translated pledge
any verification address other than the one printed on the certificate

rules.rule: Never say or suggest that you, a project or any contributor was paid from Purpose Fees, or that your credit earned you money.
rules.reason: The statutes bar it (Art. 3 para. 1 item 2 and Art. 5 para. 2): contributors are never paid from Purpose Fees for a contribution.

rules.rule: Speak of your choices among the categories only as recorded choices: never say that you gave, sent, directed or routed money, that a charity got money because of you, or that your choice was a donation or a gift.
rules.reason: Under the statutes (Art. 8 para. 4) a contributor's choice is advisory: it is recorded, published in aggregate and never binds the Association, which allocates under its published rule.

rules.rule: Never compare yourself with other contributors or say where you stand among them.
rules.reason: Purpose Source publishes no ranking of people and keeps each person's measure of credit private, so a comparison could not be checked and would invite gaming the credit.

rules.rule: When you cite this certificate, claim only what it and its lines state: no claim that your own work does good or helps people, no other social-impact claim, and no green, climate or sustainability claim.
rules.reason: A claim made with this certificate borrows its trust, and the certificate proves credit and nothing more. Where you use it to market your work or services, Directive (EU) 2024/825 bans generic environmental claims and counts social characteristics among what a misleading claim can concern, and Swiss unfair-competition law forbids misleading statements.

rules.rule: Never present the certificate as an endorsement, approval, rating or licence of you or your code by Purpose Source.
rules.reason: It records credit computed from a project's history; Purpose Source made no check of the quality of the work.

rules.rule: Offer no place to check the certificate other than purposesource.org/verify and your certificate's own address under it.
rules.reason: One address is what makes a forged certificate or badge easy to spot.

rules.rule: Say where Purpose Fees go only by linking purposesource.org/trust/money or by quoting the Association's pledge exactly as written: never shorten, paraphrase or translate it.
rules.reason: The pledge is stated in one form only, with its capped costs beside it (statutes Art. 5 para. 5); a share of the fees taken out of its sentence says more than the pledge does.

rules.rule: Say that Purpose Source software asks the larger companies that rely on it to give something back only together with the link to where the money goes, purposesource.org/trust/money, as the lines do; never say that you or your work supports charities.
rules.reason: The give-back can be checked only against the published money record, and the certificate records your work, not a gift of yours. A charity claim about a person cannot be checked against that record, so it is the vague claim these rules exist to stop, as kit-1 keeps it out of an organisation's claims too.

rules.rule: Use the words of your own certificate: the volunteer words only with a certificate that prints them, and never call yourself a volunteer on these projects with a certificate that does not.
rules.reason: The volunteer words rest on the holder's own answer in their account, given before the certificate was issued, which Purpose Source does not check; a certificate issued without that answer uses the contributor words, and a claim may say no more than the certificate it cites.
